newsitem.title: UK: R-OPTIONS - Tarmac features in thin market.
newsitem.headline: R-OPTIONS - Tarmac features in thin market.

text.p: Only a handful of share option contracts were traded by midday as the market wound down for the Christmas holidays, dealers said.
"It has been as dead as a doornail. What trades there have been are small," one dealer said.
"With the FTSE only open for a half-day on Tuesday, it will be quiet again tomorrow." The London share market closes at 1230 GMT on Christmas Eve, Tuesday, December 24.
The only trade of any size was in Tarmac Plc where one broker bought 2,000 September 100 calls -- 1,000 at 9p and 1,000 at 9-1/2p.
Tarmac shares were trading at 95-1/2p, up 1-1/2p on the day by 1215 GMT.
Elsewhere, a synthetic long was established in British Telecom Plc when a broker sold 500 May 390 puts at 16p while buying 500 May 420 calls at 13p.
When a person buys a call and sells a put, he sets up a position that is equivalent to owning the stock.
This deal left the broker with a net 3p, less commissions. If BT's share price is anywhere between 390p and 420p at expiration, the broker will make a profit of 3p, equal to the initial credit.
If BT rises far enough, profits can be generated on both the long call and the short put. The risk occurs if BT drops below 390p, producing losses on both the short put and the long call.
Another synthetic long was created in Cable & Wireless Plc when a broker sold 500 April 460 puts at 12p and bought 500 April 500 calls at 19p.
Cable & Wireless shares were up 8-1/2p at 485p.
